dedupe_keys.name: associative analysis of inefficiencies and station activity levels in emergency response

description: DAPI is an implemented tool that identifies potential response bottlenecks from the spatial distribution of ambulance responses and assesses them against inferred dispatch-station activity. Its application uses medical-emergency responses across mainland Portugal. The reported association between slower or inefficient responses and high activity at nearer stations supports operational investigation; it does not by itself prove causality. This analytical decision tool is separate from the related emergency-data consolidation component. The source does not establish public raw emergency records, code distribution, or a current operational service endpoint. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with open document or data access and licence label cc-by-4.0. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened.
